site.name: OpenAlt
site.tagline: The open source alternative to the tools you already pay for

tools.name: Notion
tools.summary: All-in-one workspace combining notes, documents, wikis and databases.

alternatives.why: Closest 1:1 replacement: docs, databases and kanban in one offline-first app.
Docs and whiteboard on the same canvas; better than Notion for visual thinking.
Outliner built on local Markdown files you actually own.
Block-based notes with a built-in database and no subscription.

tools.name: Evernote
tools.summary: Note capture with web clipping and notebook organisation.

alternatives.why: The standard Evernote replacement: end-to-end encryption, web clipper, sync you choose.
If your notes are thinking rather than filing, an outliner beats a notebook.
Local-first with strong block references and backlinks.
Markdown editor with citation support; good for research writing.

tools.name: Confluence
tools.summary: Team wiki and documentation space attached to Jira.

alternatives.why: The cleanest wiki experience of the bunch; fast search, nice editor.
Confluence-like spaces and permissions without Atlassian's weight.
Mature, stable, integrates with almost any auth provider.
Books, chapters and pages. Simple mental model that never confuses writers.

tools.name: Google Docs
tools.summary: Browser word processor with real-time collaboration.

alternatives.why: Full office suite, collaborative editing, self-hostable, strong docx fidelity.
LibreOffice in the browser. Best compatibility with existing .docx files.
Real-time collaborative text with zero ceremony. Great for drafting.
End-to-end encrypted docs, sheets and slides.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.summary: Local Markdown knowledge base with a graph and plugin ecosystem.

alternatives.why: Closest in spirit: local files, outliner, backlinks, plugins.
Local-first with a database layer Obsidian lacks.
If you want databases alongside notes and a Notion-like UI.

tools.name: Linear
tools.summary: Fast issue tracking built around keyboard-driven workflows.

alternatives.why: Cycles, modules and issues with a UI close enough that switching takes an afternoon.
Issues, docs, HR and CRM in one self-hosted platform.
Lightweight task manager, single binary, lists and kanban and Gantt.
Agile-first with epics and sprints. Older but battle-tested.

tools.name: Jira
tools.summary: Issue and sprint tracking with deep customisation.

alternatives.why: The most complete Jira replacement: work packages, Gantt, budgets, roadmaps.
Agile-native: backlog, sprints, burndown without plugin hunting.
Twenty years of stability. Ugly, unkillable, plugin-rich.
Modern alternative if your team never used Jira's advanced config anyway.

tools.name: Trello
tools.summary: Kanban boards with cards, lists and simple automation.

alternatives.why: Closest Trello clone: boards, lists, cards, real-time updates.
The original open source kanban. Swimplanes, checklists, integrations.
Kanban plus Gantt and calendar views; more than a board.
Boards that live next to your chat; good if you already run Mattermost.

tools.name: Asana
tools.summary: Task and project tracking with timelines and dependencies.

alternatives.why: Task boards and sprints with a similar feel.
Handles dependencies and timelines better than most paid tools.
Much lighter, single binary, no per-seat cost.
If your Asana use is really just issues and owners.

tools.name: monday.com
tools.summary: Colourful work OS built on configurable boards.

alternatives.why: Cleaner board and issue model without the spreadsheet sprawl.
Configurable work packages cover most monday use cases.
Multiple apps (issues, CRM, docs) sharing one data model.
Simpler and faster if you never used monday's automations.

tools.name: ClickUp
tools.summary: Everything app: tasks, docs, goals, time tracking.

alternatives.why: Does the 20% of ClickUp people actually use, and much faster.
Genuinely multi-app: issues, docs, CRM, HR in one.
Tasks and lists without the feature maze.
When you need the heavy project-management half of ClickUp.

tools.name: Airtable
tools.summary: Spreadsheet-database hybrid with views and automations.

alternatives.why: The most direct Airtable replacement: views, filters, forms, API on top of any SQL database.
Polished UI, self-hostable, strong formula and view support.
Postgres-backed with a real spreadsheet feel at scale.
Rows, views and plugins; good for teams replacing Airtable wholesale.

tools.name: Slack
tools.summary: Channel-based team messaging with integrations and huddles.

alternatives.why: Most mature Slack replacement: channels, threads, playbooks, big integration ecosystem.
Slack-style UI plus omnichannel: web, email and social in one inbox.
Threaded conversations that stay readable at scale. Best for async teams.
Matrix client: federated, encrypted, not owned by one company.

tools.name: Discord
tools.summary: Voice, video and community chat built around servers.

alternatives.why: Spacebar: a Discord-compatible server, so existing clients and bots work.
Revolt's client: Discord-shaped UX, self-hostable, modern stack.
Matrix gives you federation and encryption Discord will never add.
If you need channels plus real support tooling.

tools.name: Figma
tools.summary: Browser-based interface design with real-time multiplayer editing.

alternatives.why: The only true Figma competitor: design and code in one file, self-hostable.
Hand-drawn diagrams and wireframes, far faster than Figma for early thinking.
Embeddable infinite canvas. A toolkit rather than a finished design app.

tools.name: Sketch
tools.summary: Mac-native interface design with symbols and libraries.

alternatives.why: Cross-platform, browser-based, and free of the Mac requirement.
Good for sketching flows and systems before committing to a design file.
Wireframes that look intentionally rough, which is usually an advantage.

tools.name: Photoshop
tools.summary: Raster image editing and compositing.

alternatives.why: The strongest open source painting and raster editor; excellent brush engine.
Node-based vector and raster editing; a different, faster workflow for composites.
For the vector half of what people use Photoshop for.

tools.name: Illustrator
tools.summary: Vector illustration and logo design.

alternatives.why: The long-standing vector editor; SVG-native and scriptable.
Modern node-based vector tool with a much better UI than Inkscape.
Handles vector layers alongside raster for illustration work.

tools.name: Canva
tools.summary: Template-driven design for non-designers.

alternatives.why: Real design tooling without the per-seat model; templates are your own.
Good for producing consistent graphics once, then reusing them.
For the diagram-and-flow half of what people use Canva for.

tools.name: Excel
tools.summary: Spreadsheet with formulas, pivot tables and macros.

alternatives.why: The full suite, best formula coverage, and it opens .xlsx without drama.
Closest to Excel's modern UI; strong compatibility and collaboration.
Browser editing on top of LibreOffice's engine.

tools.name: Microsoft Word
tools.summary: Desktop word processor and the .docx standard.

alternatives.why: Opens and saves .docx reliably; the default answer for a reason.
Ribbon UI that Word users recognise immediately.
LibreOffice in the browser for teams that never install software.
When the document is really a shared draft, not a formatted deliverable.

tools.name: PowerPoint
tools.summary: Slide decks with transitions and presenter tools.

alternatives.why: Impress handles .pptx and is included in the same install as Writer and Calc.
Best-looking deck editor of the open source options.
Browser-based decks for teams that collaborate live.

tools.name: Gmail
tools.summary: Webmail with search, labels and a large integration surface.

alternatives.why: Battle-tested webmail; runs on any IMAP server you control.
Desktop client that feels modern; good Gmail-shaped habits.
Not just a client: the mail server itself, in containers.

tools.name: Outlook
tools.summary: Mail, calendar and contacts in one desktop and web client.

alternatives.why: Fast desktop mail with unified inboxes.
Reliable webmail you host yourself.
Full mail stack with calendar and contacts via SOGo.

tools.name: 1Password
tools.summary: Password manager with sharing, passkeys and audit logs.

alternatives.why: Feature-complete and self-hostable, with clients on every platform.
Lightweight Bitwarden-compatible server. Runs on a Raspberry Pi.
Fully offline, file-based vault. No server to breach.

tools.name: LastPass
tools.summary: Cloud password manager with browser extensions.

alternatives.why: Fastest migration path; works with existing Bitwarden apps.
The full platform if you want organisations and audit trails.
If you would rather not trust any vendor after a breach.

tools.name: Dropbox
tools.summary: Cloud file sync and sharing across devices.

alternatives.why: Files, sharing, calendar, contacts and office integration in one platform.
Focused on reliable sync and file locking; faster than Nextcloud on large libraries.
Peer-to-peer, no server, no account. Devices sync directly.

tools.name: Google Drive
tools.summary: Cloud storage tied to Google's office suite.

alternatives.why: The closest full replacement, including the office suite via Collabora.
Better raw file sync performance and versioning.
For people who want the files but not the cloud.

tools.name: Google Analytics
tools.summary: Web analytics with event tracking and attribution.

alternatives.why: Privacy-first, cookie-free, one script tag. Answers the questions GA buries.
Lightweight self-hosted analytics with a clean dashboard.
Full GA-style depth, on your own server, with heatmaps and funnels.
Product analytics plus session replay and feature flags.

tools.name: Mixpanel
tools.summary: Product analytics focused on funnels and retention.

alternatives.why: The closest full replacement: events, funnels, cohorts, replay, flags.
If you only need traffic and referrers, this is far cheaper to run.
Simple event tracking without the product-analytics overhead.

tools.name: Hotjar
tools.summary: Session recordings, heatmaps and on-site surveys.

alternatives.why: Self-hosted session replay with DOM inspection and network logs.
Replay tied to the same events as your funnels, so you can act on it.
The recording engine itself, if you want to build your own tooling.

tools.name: Segment
tools.summary: Customer data pipeline routing events to many destinations.

alternatives.why: Self-hosted event pipeline that speaks the Segment API, so existing SDKs work.
Closest architectural match: warehouse-first CDP with the same event model.
If you would rather keep events and analysis in one system.

tools.name: Zoom
tools.summary: Video meetings with recording and breakout rooms.

alternatives.why: The default self-hosted answer: no account needed for guests, scales well.
Built for teaching: whiteboard, breakout rooms, recording.
WebRTC infrastructure if you want to build video into your own product.

tools.name: Loom
tools.summary: Quick screen recordings with shareable links.

alternatives.why: The closest Loom replacement: fast screen capture with shareable links.
Heavier, but records anything and streams it too.

tools.name: Postman
tools.summary: API client with collections, environments and mocking.

alternatives.why: Collections stored as plain files in your repo. No cloud, no login.
Browser-based, fast, works without an account.
Mature client with strong GraphQL and gRPC support.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.summary: AI code completion and chat inside the editor.

alternatives.why: Bring your own model; works across VS Code and JetBrains.
Self-hosted completion server. Your code never leaves your infrastructure.
Agentic coding in the editor with explicit approval for every action.
Terminal-first pair programmer that commits its own changes.

tools.name: Vercel
tools.summary: Frontend hosting with preview deployments and edge functions.

alternatives.why: Deploy anything from Git with previews, on your own server.
The original single-server Heroku replacement. Boring and reliable.
Web UI over Docker with one-click apps.

tools.name: Heroku
tools.summary: Platform-as-a-service with git push deploys.

alternatives.why: Closest match: git push to deploy, buildpacks, single server.
More modern UI and broader support than Dokku.
Easiest to hand to a non-DevOps teammate.

tools.name: Sentry
tools.summary: Error tracking with stack traces and release health.

alternatives.why: The product itself is open source. Self-host and keep the same SDKs.
Errors plus session replay in one self-hosted tool.
Strong on the replay side; useful when errors are hard to reproduce.

tools.name: Datadog
tools.summary: Infrastructure monitoring, APM, logs and dashboards.

alternatives.why: Real-time infrastructure metrics with almost no setup.
Dashboards over any data source; the visual layer most teams want.
Metrics collection and alerting that everything else integrates with.
Closest single-binary Datadog replacement: traces, metrics and logs.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.summary: Connect apps with trigger-action automations.

alternatives.why: Visual automations with real code steps when the GUI runs out.
Simpler than n8n, MIT licensed, easy to extend with pieces.
Scripts as workflows; better when automation is really engineering.
Agent-based automation that has aged surprisingly well.

tools.name: Retool
tools.summary: Build internal tools by dragging components onto a canvas.

alternatives.why: The most direct Retool competitor: drag-and-drop UI over your data.
Clean alternative with a strong component library.
Faster for simple CRUD apps; good for non-developers.

tools.name: Calendly
tools.summary: Booking pages that respect calendar availability.

alternatives.why: The full Calendly replacement: team routing, payments, workflows.
Group scheduling without accounts for participants.
Appointment booking for a business with staff and services.

tools.name: Intercom
tools.summary: Live chat, help centre and customer messaging.

alternatives.why: The strongest open source answer: shared inbox, live chat, help centre.
Full helpdesk with SLAs and ticket routing.
Lightweight shared mailbox. Replaces the email half of Intercom cheaply.

tools.name: HubSpot
tools.summary: CRM with marketing, sales and service hubs.

alternatives.why: Modern CRM built the way HubSpot should have been; actively developed.
Mature CRM with custom entities and workflow automation.
Deep sales pipeline features, widely used in larger teams.
CRM plus accounting, inventory and HR in one suite.

tools.name: Salesforce
tools.summary: Enterprise CRM with deep customisation and reporting.

alternatives.why: Modern data model with a much shorter time-to-first-record.
Custom entities and relationships cover a lot of Salesforce config.
Established, extensible and built for sales teams rather than admins.
When CRM is one module of a larger business system.

tools.name: Mailchimp
tools.summary: Email marketing with automation and audience segmentation.

alternatives.why: Single binary newsletter and mailing list manager. Extremely fast.
Full marketing automation: campaigns, segments, lead scoring.

tools.name: Shopify
tools.summary: Hosted storefront with payments and inventory.

alternatives.why: Headless commerce with a real developer API and no platform lock-in.
GraphQL-first commerce with a strong multi-channel model.
Runs on WordPress, which most small stores already know how to manage.
TypeScript-native commerce framework for teams already in Node.

tools.name: Google Calendar
tools.summary: Shared calendars with scheduling and invites.

alternatives.why: Handles the booking half; pairs with any CalDAV calendar.
Includes a CalDAV calendar server alongside files.
When the problem is finding a time, not managing events.
